Protobuf JSON

Source: R/json.R
proto_to_json.Rd

Converts a binary message to protobuf's canonical JSON mapping and back, through upb. JSON field names are the json_names (lowerCamelCase) by default, 64-bit integers are strings, bytes are base64, and well-known types take their special JSON forms (Timestamp as an RFC 3339 string, Struct as an object, and so on).

Usage

proto_to_json(
  x,
  type,
  pool,
  emit_defaults = FALSE,
  proto_names = FALSE,
  enums = c("name", "integer"),
  parse = FALSE,
  max_size = zpb_limits$max_size,
  max_depth = zpb_limits$max_depth
)

proto_from_json(
  json,
  type,
  pool,
  ignore_unknown = FALSE,
  check_required = TRUE,
  max_size = zpb_limits$max_size
)

Arguments

x

For proto_to_json(), the binary message: a raw vector, a path or a connection.

type

The message type's full name, such as "pkg.Message".

pool

A pool from proto_pool() holding type.

emit_defaults

Whether to write fields that hold their defaults.

proto_names

Whether to use the .proto field names rather than their json_names.

enums

"name" or "integer": how enum values are written.

parse

Whether to return the JSON parsed into an R value by zujson::json_parse() rather than as text.

max_size

The largest input accepted, in bytes. upb's memory for the decode is also capped, at a multiple of the input's size that the message type sets: the most a message of that type could legitimately need.

max_depth

The deepest nesting accepted: how many levels of messages within messages, the top-level message being level 0. A message holding a message holding a message is depth 2. A map entry counts as a level too, as upb counts it, so a message reached through a map is two levels down. At most 1000, so that hostile input cannot exhaust the C stack.

json

Protobuf JSON for one message: a single string of JSON text, or an R value to write as JSON with zujson::json_write().

ignore_unknown

Whether to skip JSON fields the type does not define, rather than fail.

check_required

Whether a missing proto2 required field is an error.

Value

proto_to_json(): a single string, or with parse = TRUE an R value. proto_from_json(): the message as a raw vector, encoded deterministically.

Details

Any messages convert only when the type they pack is in the pool.

JSON meets R values through zujson, which must be installed for it: proto_to_json(parse = TRUE) returns zujson::json_parse()'s R value, and proto_from_json() takes an R value as well as JSON text, written with zujson::json_write(). There, a length-1 vector is a JSON scalar: give a repeated field of one element as I(x) or list(x).

Examples

pool <- proto_pool()
raw <- proto_encode(
  as.POSIXct("2026-10-25 12:00:00", tz = "UTC"),
  "google.protobuf.Timestamp", pool
)
json <- proto_to_json(raw, "google.protobuf.Timestamp", pool)
json
#> [1] "\"2026-10-25T12:00:00Z\""
identical(proto_from_json(json, "google.protobuf.Timestamp", pool), raw)
#> [1] TRUE
